relevance_reason: Systematic review of the treatments used in GACR patients and their reported effects on ornithine levels. It is relevant to the clinical management section.

findings.statement: Balfoort et al. (2021) carried out a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines of therapeutic interventions in GACR. They identified 33 studies covering 107 patients, mostly case reports (27) or case series (4), and found no randomized controlled trials or large cohort studies. Protein-restricted diets lowered ornithine levels by 16.0 to 91.2%. Pyridoxine responsiveness was reported in 30% of the included mutations. Lysine supplementation decreased ornithine levels by 21 to 34%. Other treatments reported were creatine or creatine precursor supplementation and proline supplementation.
quotes: A total of 33 studies (n = 107 patients) met the inclusion criteria. Most studies were designed as case reports (n = 27) or case series (n = 4). No randomised controlled trials or large cohort studies were found.

Protein-restricted diets lowered ornithine levels ranging from 16.0-91.2%. Pyridoxine responsiveness was reported in 30% of included mutations. Lysine supplementation decreased ornithine levels with 21-34%.
Treatments applied were protein-restricted diets, pyridoxine supplementation, creatine or creatine precursor supplementation, l-lysine supplementation, and proline supplementation.

findings.statement: Balfoort et al. (2021) concluded that a protein-restricted diet, pyridoxine supplementation (depending on the variant), and/or lysine supplementation can reduce ornithine levels. Because the included studies lacked predefined clinical outcome measures and structured follow-up, the authors could not draw conclusions about clinical effectiveness. They noted that there is no curative treatment and no international treatment protocol.
quotes: Based primarily on case reports ornithine levels can be reduced by using a protein restricted diet, pyridoxine supplementation (variation-dependent) and/or lysine supplementation.
The lack of pre-defined clinical outcome measures and structural follow-up in all included studies impeded conclusions on clinical effectiveness.
No international treatment protocol is available.

findings.statement: Balfoort et al. (2021) described GACR as a rare inborn error of amino acid metabolism caused by biallelic variants in the OAT gene. It is characterized by vision decline in early life that eventually leads to complete blindness, and by high plasma ornithine levels.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (GACR) is a rare inborn error of amino acid metabolism caused by bi-allelic variations in OAT.
GACR is characterised by vision decline in early life eventually leading to complete blindness, and high plasma ornithine levels.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows the paper is about carriers (heterozygotes) of the gene for Fuchs gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, linked in the title to Alder's anomaly. No data could be extracted.

findings.statement: FRANCOIS et al. (1960) studied carriers of the gene for Fuchs gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (atrophia gyrata chorioideae et retinae). The title links the condition to Alder's anomaly.
quotes: [Conductors of the gene of Fuchs' atrophia gyrata chorioideae et retinae (Alder's anomaly)].

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

relevance_reason: Clinical cohort study describing peripheral nervous system involvement in 40 patients with gyrate atrophy, which extends the phenotype.

findings.statement: Peltola et al. (2002) looked for peripheral nervous system involvement in 40 patients with gyrate atrophy (mean age 31.6 +/- 16.3 years; range 5 to 74 years) using neurography, quantitative sensory threshold testing, and evoked potential testing. Neurography was abnormal in 21 patients (53%), and the abnormalities were associated with patient age and with the severity of the ophthalmologic changes. Quantitative sensory threshold testing showed abnormal large-fiber function in 7 patients (18%) and abnormal small-fiber function in 4 patients (10%). Somatosensory and brainstem auditory evoked potential responses were abolished in 5 patients.
quotes: The authors searched evidence of peripheral nervous involvement in 40 patients with GA (mean age 31.6 +/- 16.3 years; range 5 to 74 years) by using neurography, quantitative sensory threshold testing, and evoked potential testing.
Neurography revealed abnormalities in 21 (53%) of the patients. The abnormalities associated with the severity of the ophthalmologic changes and the age of the patients.

With quantitative sensory threshold testing, abnormal large-fiber function was found in seven (18%) and abnormal small-fiber function was found in four (10%) patients. Somatosensory evoked potential and brainstem auditory evoked potential responses were abolished in five patients.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of peripheral nervous system electrophysiology

findings.statement: Peltola et al. (2002) described gyrate atrophy as an inborn error of amino acid metabolism caused by mutations in ornithine aminotransferase. Its features are hyperornithinemia, progressive centripetal loss of vision, minor CNS abnormalities, and type II muscle fiber atrophy with accumulation of tubular aggregates. From the peripheral nerve findings, they concluded that gyrate atrophy is a systemic disease that affects the peripheral nervous system as well as the CNS.
quotes: GA is an inborn error of amino acid metabolism caused by mutations in the enzyme ornithine aminotransferase. Patients with GA have hyperornithinemia, progressive centripetal loss of vision, minor CNS abnormalities, and type II muscle fiber atrophy with accumulation of tubular aggregates.
These findings of peripheral nervous system involvement in GA suggest that GA is a systemic disease affecting not only CNS but also the peripheral nervous system.

relevance_reason: Reports the long-term results of treating patients with gyrate atrophy using an arginine-restricted diet, which belongs in the clinical management section.

findings.statement: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (2002) reported 2 pairs of sibs with gyrate atrophy who had been on an arginine-restricted diet to lower plasma ornithine for 16 to 17 years. In each pair, the younger sib started the diet at an earlier age than the older sib, and the younger sib's chorioretinal lesions progressed more slowly. The authors concluded that long-term, substantial reduction of plasma ornithine, if begun early, may appreciably slow the progression of chorioretinal lesions and, to a lesser extent, the progressive loss of retinal function.
quotes: Natural history study of 2 pairs of siblings with gyrate atrophy treated with an arginine-restricted diet.

After 16 to 17 years of receiving an arginine-restricted diet, the younger sibling in each pair, who was prescribed the diet at an earlier age than the older sibling, demonstrated a slower progression of lesions compared with the older sibling.

If started at an early age, long-term substantial reduction of plasma ornithine levels may appreciably slow the progression of the chorioretinal lesions and, to a lesser extent, the progressive loss of retinal function in patients with gyrate atrophy.

relevance_reason: Natural history of visual function decline in gyrate atrophy patients being considered for gene replacement therapy; relevant to the clinical course and clinical management.

findings.statement: Caruso et al. (2001) assessed the course of change in visual function in 5 patients with gyrate atrophy before a gene replacement therapy clinical trial, using visual field sensitivity and electroretinogram amplitude as outcome variables and calculating their half-lives. Over 4 to 6 years of follow-up, median visual field half-lives were 17.0 years by static perimetry and 11.4 years by kinetic perimetry, and median electroretinogram half-lives were 16.0 years for the maximal response and 10.7 years for the flicker response. The authors concluded that visual function frequently declines slowly.
quotes: To assess the course of change of visual function outcome variables in 5 patients with gyrate atrophy before a gene replacement therapy clinical trial.

median visual field half-lives were 17.0 years (static perimetry) and 11.4 years (kinetic perimetry). Median electroretinogram half-lives were 16.0 years (maximal response) and 10.7 years (flicker response).
The course of the decline of visual function outcome variables is frequently slow.

findings.statement: Caruso et al. (2001) concluded that, because visual function in gyrate atrophy often declines slowly, a long-term clinical trial would be needed to assess whether gene replacement therapy preserves visual function.
quotes: Thus, a long-term clinical trial would be required to assess the efficacy of the intervention in the preservation of visual function.

relevance_reason: Mouse model of OAT deficiency showing arginine-restricted diet lowers ornithine and prevents retinal degeneration; informs pathogenesis and management of GA.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2000) maintained Oat-null (Oat -/-) mice, produced by gene targeting, on an arginine-restricted diet for 12 months and monitored them by plasma amino acid measurement, electroretinography, and retinal histologic and ultrastructural studies. The diet substantially reduced plasma ornithine levels and completely prevented retinal degeneration in the Oat -/- mice.
quotes: we used an arginine-restricted diet to maintain long term reduction of ornithine in a mouse model of OAT-deficiency (Oat(-/-)) produced by gene targeting
We found that an arginine-restricted diet substantially reduces plasma ornithine levels and completely prevents retinal degeneration in Oat(-/-).

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2000) concluded from the prevention of retinal degeneration by an arginine-restricted diet in Oat -/- mice that ornithine accumulation is a necessary factor in the pathophysiology of the retinal degeneration in gyrate atrophy, and that restoring OAT activity in the retina is not required for effective treatment.
quotes: This result indicates that ornithine accumulation is a necessary factor in the pathophysiology of the retinal degeneration in GA and that restoration of OAT activity in retina is not required for effective treatment of GA.

relevance_reason: Describes central nervous system involvement (brain MRI and EEG abnormalities) in a cohort of patients with gyrate atrophy with hyperornithinemia, adding to the phenotype.

findings.statement: Valtonen et al. (1999) studied central nervous system involvement in 23 untreated patients with gyrate atrophy (mean age 32 +/- 18 years) and compared them with age-matched healthy controls. Brain MRI showed degenerative white matter lesions in 50% of patients, and 70% had premature atrophic changes, with a striking increase in the number of Virchow (perivascular) spaces. Of the patients who had an EEG, 58% had abnormal slow background activity, focal lesions, or high-amplitude beta rhythm (more than 50 microV). The EEG findings were not associated with the MRI changes or with the patients' age or sex. The authors concluded that early degenerative and atrophic brain changes and an abnormal EEG are features of gyrate atrophy, in addition to the known eye and muscle manifestations.
quotes: We compared 23 untreated GA patients with age-matched healthy controls, and with 9 patients who had received creatine or creatine precursor supplementation daily for several years.

Brain MRI revealed degenerative lesions in the white matter in 50% of the GA patients, and 70% of the patients had premature atrophic changes, with a striking increase in the number of Virchow's spaces.
Of the patients whose EEG was recorded, 58% had abnormal slow background activity, focal lesions or high-amplitude beta rhythm (> 50 microV).

phenotypes.text: degenerative white matter lesions on brain MRI
abnormal EEG with slow background activity, focal lesions or high-amplitude beta rhythm

findings.statement: Valtonen et al. (1999) found that the brain MRI and EEG findings in 9 patients with gyrate atrophy who had taken creatine or creatine precursor supplements daily for several years did not differ from those of 23 untreated patients.
quotes: We compared 23 untreated GA patients with age-matched healthy controls, and with 9 patients who had received creatine or creatine precursor supplementation daily for several years.
The MRI or EEG findings of the patients on creatine supplementation did not differ from those of the untreated group.

findings.statement: Valtonen et al. (1999) noted that the retinal and choroidal degeneration and the type II muscle fiber atrophy with tubular aggregates in gyrate atrophy have been suggested to be caused by a deficiency of phosphocreatine induced by hyperornithinemia. Because guanidinoacetate methyltransferase deficiency, another disorder of creatine metabolism, causes abnormal brain MRI and EEG findings, they studied the central nervous system in gyrate atrophy, which appears to involve a milder degree of phosphocreatine deficiency.
quotes: These findings have been suggested to be mediated by hyperornithinaemia-induced deficiency of high-energy creatine phosphate.
we investigated the central nervous system involvement in GA, which seems to be associated with a milder degree of phosphocreatine deficiency

relevance_reason: Clinical study characterizing skeletal muscle involvement (biopsy, CT, MRI) in 7 patients with gyrate atrophy.

findings.statement: Valtonen et al. (1996) examined the thigh muscles of 7 patients with gyrate atrophy using semi-open conchotome muscle biopsies, CT, and ultralow-field (0.02 T) MRI. Type 2 muscle fiber atrophy was found in all biopsy samples and tubular aggregates in 6 of 7 samples.
quotes: the thigh muscles of 7 patients with GA were examined using semi-open conchotome muscle biopsies, computed tomography (CT) and ultralow-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at 0.02 T
Type 2 muscle fibre atrophy was found in all biopsy samples (100%) and tubular aggregates in 6 of the 7 samples studied (87%).

findings.statement: Valtonen et al. (1996) found that CT density of thigh muscle was increased in the only child studied, decreased in 3 elderly patients, and normal in the remaining 3. Mean MRI T1 relaxation times were decreased in patients compared with 6 healthy controls (135 vs 157 ms, p = 0.002), whereas T2 was slightly but not significantly increased; the authors concluded that thigh muscles of GA patients universally show changes on CT and MRI, but relaxation time measurements gave little additional information on muscle metabolism.
quotes: The CT density of the muscle tissue was increased in the only child of the study, decreased in 3 elderly subjects, and normal in the remaining 3 patients.
Mean T1 relaxation times of the patients were decreased (135 +/- 5 ms) as compared to those of 6 healthy controls (157 +/- 12 ms) (p = 0.002).

Our findings suggest that the thigh muscles of the patients with GA universally show changes in CT and MRI studies, but relaxation time measurements gave little additional information on the muscle metabolism.

relevance_reason: Reports an Oat-knockout mouse model of gyrate atrophy and transient neonatal hypoornithinemia in one human infant with GA.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (1995) used gene targeting to produce OAT-deficient mice. As neonates, the mice had hypoornithinemia and died, but short-term arginine supplementation rescued them. After weaning they developed hyperornithinemia like that of human GA patients. Over several months they developed a retinal degeneration involving the photoreceptors and pigment epithelium, and the authors concluded that OAT-deficient mice appear to be an excellent model of human GA.
quotes: Surprisingly, OAT-deficient mice produced by gene targeting exhibit neonatal hypoornithinaemia and lethality, rescuable by short-term arginine supplementation.
Post-weaning, these mice develop hyperornithinaemia similar to human GA patients.
Over several months, OAT-deficient mice develop a retinal degeneration with involvement of photoreceptors and pigment epithelium. OAT-deficient mice appear to be an excellent model of human GA.

phenotypes.text: retinal degeneration involving photoreceptors and pigment epithelium

findings.statement: Following the mouse findings, Wang et al. (1995) studied one human infant with GA and found transient hypoornithinemia. They concluded that the OAT reaction plays opposite roles in neonatal and adult mammals.
quotes: Subsequent studies in one human GA infant also showed transient hypoornithinaemia.
Thus, the OAT reaction plays opposite roles in neonatal and adult mammals.

relevance_reason: Reports how one patient with gyrate atrophy responded to a low-arginine diet that lowered plasma ornithine, with visual function improving.

findings.statement: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (1980) reported a female patient with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina who was treated with an arginine-deficient diet. Over 20 months, the diet lowered her plasma ornithine concentration fivefold. About 15 months after starting the diet, she noticed her vision had improved. The electroretinogram, dark adaptation and color vision also improved, mostly in rod function and to a lesser extent in cone function. The authors called the results preliminary but suggested that lowering plasma ornithine with a low-arginine diet is beneficial in this disease.
quotes: In a patient with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, an arginine-deficient diet has reduced plasma ornithine concentration fivefold during the past 20 months.
This has been documented by improvements in the electroretinogram, dark-adaptation, and color vision. The improvement involves rod and, to a lesser extent, cone function.
The results, although preliminary and limited to a single patient, suggest that reduction of plasma ornithine with a low arginine diet is beneficial in this disease.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina

relevance_reason: Biochemical study in gyrate atrophy patients showing that high ornithine inhibits guanidinoacetate/creatine synthesis; proposes a pathogenic mechanism.

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1980) gave intravenous arginine to 6 patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina and 6 controls. Serum arginine curves were similar in the two groups, but the rise in serum ornithine was more than 3 times greater in patients. The mean plasma ornithine half-time was 360 min in patients versus 97 min in controls, and patients cleared ornithine from the extracellular fluid significantly more slowly.
quotes: We administered intravenous arginine to six patients and six controls to study in vivo inhibition by high ornithine concentrations of arginine-glycine transamidinase, the rate-limiting enzyme in creatine synthesis.
The increment in serum ornithine was more than three times as great in patients as in controls. The mean half-times in plasma ornithine were 360 and 97 min, respectively.
In the patients, the metabolic clearance of ornithine from the extracellular fluid was significantly delayed.

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1980) found that after an arginine load, urinary guanidinoacetate excretion rose sharply in all controls, more so in females. Patients with gyrate atrophy always excreted less guanidinoacetate than controls, with highly significant differences within each sex. Differences in creatine excretion were less marked.
quotes: Urinary guanidinoacetate excretion rose markedly in all controls, the excretion rate being higher in females.
The patients always excreted less than the controls, the differences within the sexes being highly significant. Differences in creatine excretion after administration were less marked.

phenotypes.text: reduced urinary guanidinoacetate excretion after arginine load

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1980) concluded that in patients with gyrate atrophy, high ornithine concentrations inhibit the formation of guanidinoacetate, creatine, and possibly phosphocreatine at the transamidination step (arginine-glycine transamidinase). They suggested that a deficiency of high-energy phosphates may underlie the eye and muscle atrophies.
quotes: We conclude that in gyrate atrophy patients, formation of guanidinoacetate, creatine, and possibly phosphocreatine is inhibited at the transaminidation step by the high concentrations of ornithine.
Deficiency of the high-energy phosphates may underlie the pathogenesis of the eye and muscle atrophies.

relevance_reason: The paper describes 4 patients with gyrate atrophy and hyperornithinemia. It covers OKT deficiency, the response to vitamin B6, muscle histology and carrier studies.

findings.statement: Kennaway et al. (1980) described 4 patients with hyperornithinemia and gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina. Histochemical staining of punch muscle biopsies showed intracellular inclusions in type 2 muscle fibers, and electron microscopy showed tubular aggregates about 60 nm in diameter next to the sarcoplasmic membrane.
quotes: Four patients with hyperomithinemia and gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina age described.
Histochemical staining of punch muscle biopsies showed intracellular inclusions in type 2 muscle fibers.
Tubular aggregates, approximately 60 nm in diameter and adjacent to the sarcoplasmic membrane, were seen on electron microscopy.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina
tubular aggregates in type 2 muscle fibers

findings.statement: Kennaway et al. (1980) found deficient ornithine ketoacid aminotransferase (OKT) activity in cultured skin fibroblasts from all 4 patients. Obligate heterozygotes had about half-normal OKT activity. In 1 patient, an oral glucose tolerance test caused marked changes in serum ornithine and lysine levels, along with mild glucose intolerance.
quotes: Deficient activity of ornithine ketoacid aminotransferase (OKT) in cultured skin fibroblasts was documented in all four patients. Approximately half-normal levels were found in obligate heterozygotes.
Oral glucose tolerance testing in one patient resulted in marked changes in serum ornithine and lysine concentrations, in addition to mild glucose intolerance.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts

findings.statement: Kennaway et al. (1980) documented an in vivo response to vitamin B6 in 3 of 4 patients: oral B6 supplementation significantly lowered fasting serum ornithine and raised lysine. In vitro, the patients' fibroblasts showed increased OKT activity at higher pyridoxal phosphate concentrations.
quotes: In vivo response to vitamin B6 is documented in three of the four patients by significant reduction of fasting serum ornithine and increase of lysine after oral B6 supplementation.
In vitro response to B6 was manifest by increased OKT activity at increased concentrations of pyridoxal phosphate in fibroblasts from the patients.

findings.statement: Kennaway et al. (1980) found that obligate heterozygotes had a mean serum ornithine slightly above normal, but their values overlapped considerably with the normal range. Oral ornithine tolerance tests distinguished carriers from controls in only 1 of 5 cases, whereas fibroblast OKT activity in carriers was about half normal.
quotes: Obligate heterozygotes had a mean serum ornithine slightly higher than normal, but there was considerable overlap with the normal range.
Oral ornithine tolerance tests distinguished carriers from controls in only one of five cases.

relevance_reason: Reports amino acid metabolism in 4 patients with gyrate atrophy and the correction of hyperornithinemia with an arginine-restricted diet.

findings.statement: Valle et al. (1980) studied 4 patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, all of whom had hyperornithinemia. They also found elevated plasma histidine and decreased plasma lysine and branched-chain amino acids. Renal clearances of these amino acids were not raised enough to explain the low plasma levels.
quotes: Four patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina were studied, all of whom exhibited the hyperornithinemia characteristic of this disorder.
Elevated plasma histidine and diminished plasma lysine and branched-chain amino acids were also noted.
The renal clearances of these four amino acids were not sufficiently elevated to explain their low plasma levels.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal circulating branched-chain amino acid concentration

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

findings.statement: Valle et al. (1980) put 1 patient with gyrate atrophy on an arginine-deficient diet. Plasma ornithine fell steadily from 13 times normal to the upper limit of normal, and ornithinuria and lysinuria disappeared. Oral alpha-aminoisobutyric acid sped up the fall by increasing renal ornithine losses. As ornithine neared normal, plasma lysine normalized and plasma arginine became subnormal. Over 1.5 years on a 10-20 g protein diet plus essential amino acids, plasma ornithine stayed between 55 and 355 microM. The chorioretinal degeneration did not progress, and vision apparently improved.
quotes: In one subject, an arginine-deficient diet led to progressive reduction in plasma ornithine from 13 times normal to the upper limits of normal, along with the disappearance of ornithinuria and lysinuria.
Orally administered alpha-aminoisobutyric acid facilitated the fall in plasma ornithine by increasing renal losses of ornithine.

Long-term (1.5 yr) maintenance with a diet containing 10-20 g of protein plus essential amino acids served to keep plasma ornithine at between 55-355 microM; chorioretinal degeneration did not progress and vision apparently improved.

relevance_reason: Characterizes the kinetics of mutant OAT enzyme in liver from patients with gyrate atrophy, which bears directly on the disorder's biochemical basis.

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) found trace ornithine aminotransferase activity in liver tissue from 2 patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina with hyperornithinemia. The mutant enzyme's Km for ornithine was 200 mM, 50-fold higher than normal. Raising alpha-oxoglutarate and pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate to 10 times the concentrations that gave maximal activity of the normal enzyme had no effect on the mutant enzyme. Ornithine concentrations above 70 mM inhibited the normal enzyme, but the mutant enzyme showed no substrate inhibition even at 1,000 mM ornithine.
quotes: Liver tissue from two patients contained trace activity of the enzyme. The Michaelis (Km) value of the mutant enzyme for ornithine was 200 mM, 50-fold higher than normal
increasing the concentrations of alpha-oxoglutarate and pyridoxal 5'-phosphate to 10 times those giving maximal activity of the normal enzyme had no effect on the mutant enzyme
Substrate inhibition of the mutant could not be demonstrated at 1,000 mM ornithine concentration, whereas ornithine concentrations above 70 mM inhibited the normal enzyme.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

findings.statement: Based on the kinetic data, Sipilä et al. (1981) suggested that the abnormal ornithine aminotransferase in the 2 patients they studied has an altered binding site for ornithine.
quotes: The data suggest that the abnormal L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase in the two patients studied has an altered binding site for ornithine.

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) described gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina with hyperornithinemia as an autosomal recessive disease that leads to blindness and is associated with deficient ornithine aminotransferase activity.
quotes: Deficient activity of L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase is associated with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina with hyperornithinemia, an autosomal recessive disease leading to blindness.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a creatine treatment trial in patients with gyrate atrophy and proposes a pathogenic mechanism (creatine deficiency caused by hyperornithinemia).

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) gave 7 patients with gyrate atrophy 1.5 g of creatine daily as a dietary supplement. After 1 year of treatment, the diameter of type II muscle fibers increased from 34.1 +/- 7.1 to 49.9 +/- 7.0 microns (P less than 0.001), with no significant increase in type I fiber diameter. Visual-field tests showed no further constriction during therapy, and fundus photography showed slow impairment at an age otherwise associated with rapid progression. The authors described these results as promising but preliminary.
quotes: we supplemented the diet of seven patients with 1.5 g of creatine daily. During one year of this treatment the diameters of Type II muscle fibers increased from 34.1 +/- 7.1 to 49.9 +/- 7.0 micron (mean +/- S.D.) (P less than 0.001).
The visual-field tests showed no further constriction during the therapy. Fundus photography revealed slow impairment at an age otherwise associated with rapid progression of the disease.

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) proposed that part of the disease mechanism in gyrate atrophy may be deficient creatine formation caused by hyperornithinemia. They suggested this leads to a shortage of cellular phosphocreatine energy stores.
quotes: A pathogenic component of the disease may be deficient formation of creatine, caused by hyperornithinemia, which leads to a shortage of cellular phosphocreatine energy stores.

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) described gyrate atrophy as characterized by progressive constriction of the visual fields, a 10- to 20-fold elevation of plasma ornithine, and reduced ornithine aminotransferase activity. They noted that atrophy of type II muscle fibers is morphologically conspicuous but clinically unimportant, and that it progresses together with the eye disease.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina is a disease characterized by progressive constriction of visual fields, a 10-fold to 20-fold elevation in plasma ornithine, and depressed activity of L-ornithine:2 oxoacid aminotransferase.
Morphologically conspicuous but clinically unimportant atrophy of Type II muscle fibers progresses concomitantly with the eye disease.

relevance_reason: Clinical and histopathologic description of the cataract that occurs in gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.

findings.statement: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (1983) described the cataract in 9 phakic patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina. The lens opacities were located mainly along the confluence of the posterior sutures and interfered with vision because they lay in the visual axis. The authors concluded that by the second decade, cataract is a uniform finding in gyrate atrophy and appears to be unique compared with cataracts associated with other forms of retinal degeneration.
quotes: The clinical appearance of the cataract in nine phakic patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina is described.
Clinically, the lens opacities appeared primarily along the confluence of the sutures posteriorly, interfering with vision because of their location in the visual axis.
By the second decade, cataract is a uniform finding in patients with gyrate atrophy and appears to be unique as compared with cataracts associated with other forms of retinal degeneration.

phenotypes.text: reduced vision due to lens opacities in the visual axis
gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

findings.statement: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (1983) examined 3 cataractous lenses removed from patients with gyrate atrophy aged 31 to 47 years, both by gross inspection and under the microscope. On histology, the posterior suture region was filled with liquefied, degenerated lens material that resembled typical senile cataract changes.
quotes: The gross and microscopic examination of three cataractous lenses removed from patients 31 years to 47 years of age is reported.
Histologically the region of the posterior sutures was filled with liquified and degenerated lens material typical of senile cataractous changes.

phenotypes.text: liquefied, degenerated lens material at the posterior sutures

relevance_reason: Biochemical study of free amino acids in blood cells of two brothers with gyrate atrophy and hyperornithinemia, including an oral ornithine loading test.

findings.statement: Fukuda et al. (1983) measured free amino acid concentrations in erythrocytes, lymphocytes, and granulocytes from 2 brothers with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina and hyperornithinemia. Ornithine concentrations were raised in the blood cells, with the degree of elevation depending on cell type, and aspartic acid concentrations were low in erythrocytes.
quotes: measured the free amino acid concentrations in erythrocytes, lymphocytes, and granulocytes of two patients with gyrate atrophy with hyperornithinaemia
We found that ornithine concentrations were elevated in blood cells, to different degrees depending on the type of cell, and that aspartic acid concentrations were low in erythrocytes.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

findings.statement: Fukuda et al. (1983) followed free amino acid concentrations in blood cells of the 2 brothers for up to 24 hours after an oral dose of ornithine. Ornithine in blood cells peaked 2 hours after the dose and stayed high for at least 4 hours, but after 2 hours the concentration curves differed among erythrocytes, lymphocytes, and granulocytes.
quotes: We also investigated the fluctuation of free amino acid concentrations in blood cells up to 24 h after the oral administration of ornithine.

The ornithine concentration in the blood cells of the patients reached a peak 2 h after the oral administration, and remained high for at least 4 h, although after 2 h the concentration curves differed in the three types of cells.

relevance_reason: Case report showing that a low-arginine diet in a patient with hyperornithinemia and gyrate atrophy improved vision; directly relevant to clinical management.

findings.statement: McInnes et al. (1981) treated a 15-year-old patient with hyperornithinemia (plasma ornithine 0.6-1.2 mmol/l) and gyrate atrophy of the retina with a low-arginine diet. The diet lowered plasma ornithine to 0.15-0.25 mmol/l, close to the normal range. After 5 weeks of treatment, visual function improved in one eye that had been severely impaired, with no improvement, for 3 years. The improvement lasted until the patient stopped following the diet closely at 8 months, after which visual function regressed toward its pretreatment state.
quotes: A 15-year-old patient with hyperornithinaemia (0.6--1.2 mmol/l) and gyrate atrophy of the retina was given a low-arginine diet to reduce plasma ornithine to a concentration (0.15--0.25 mmol/l) near the normal range.
After five weeks of treatment, there was improvement in the visual function of one eye which had been severely impaired without improvement for 3 years.
This improved visual function was maintained until compliance with the diet deteriorated at eight months, after which visual function regressed towards pretreatment status.

phenotypes.text: severely impaired vision in one eye

findings.statement: McInnes et al. (1981) found that restricting dietary arginine too much caused hyperammonemia in their patient. They concluded that arginine is an essential amino acid in ornithine transaminase deficiency. They suggested that lowering plasma ornithine may reverse a metabolic neuroretinopathy in this disease and might also stop the retinal atrophy from progressing.
quotes: Overrestriction of dietary arginine produced hyperammonaemia, indicating that arginine is an essential aminoacid in ornithine transaminase deficiency.
These results suggest that reduction of plasma ornithine may reverse a metabolic neuroretinopathy in this disease, and offer hope that progression of the retinal atrophy can be arrested as well.

phenotypes.text: hyperammonemia with overrestriction of dietary arginine

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It shows the paper is about gene carriers of Fuchs gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, but no data can be extracted.

findings.statement: François et al. (1966) wrote about gene carriers of Fuchs gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (atrophia gyrata choroideae et retinae).
quotes: [Apropos of gene carriers of Fuch's atrophia gyrata choroideae et retinae].

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows the paper deals with the genetics of gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina with hyperornithinemia, which is this entry's subject, but no specific findings can be pulled from a title alone.

findings.statement: Takki and Simell (1974) discussed the genetic aspects of gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina with hyperornithinemia.
quotes: Genetic aspects in gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina with hyperornithinaemia.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina

relevance_reason: The title reports that raised plasma ornithine occurs with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, which is the key biochemical feature of this entry.

findings.statement: Simell and Takki (1973) reported that raised plasma ornithine occurs with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.
quotes: Raised plasma-ornithine and gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina

relevance_reason: Biochemical and complementation studies in fibroblasts from pyridoxine-responsive and non-responsive gyrate atrophy patients, suggesting allelic heterogeneity at the OAT (OKT) locus.

findings.statement: Wirtz et al. (1985) studied fibroblasts from 4 pyridoxine-responsive and 3 non-responsive patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina. Cells from responsive patients had higher ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) activity in homogenates and more incorporation of radioactivity from 14C-ornithine into protein in cultured cells in situ than cells from non-responsive patients.
quotes: Fibroblasts from four pyridoxine responsive and three non-responsive patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina have been examined.

Responsive patients had higher activity of ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) in cell homogenates and greater incorporation of radioactivity from 14C-ornithine into protein in cultured cells in situ compared to non-responsive patients.

phenotypes.text: reduced ornithine ketoacid transaminase activity in fibroblasts

findings.statement: Wirtz et al. (1985) performed complementation analysis on fused fibroblasts from the 7 patients, measuring the ratio of 14C/3H incorporation into protein after incubation in 14C-ornithine and 3H-leucine. Crosses showed no positive complementation, and the authors suggested that pyridoxine-responsive and non-responsive gyrate atrophy are caused by different allelic mutations at the same OKT locus.
quotes: Complementation analysis of the cells from these seven patients was performed, based on the ratio of incorporation of 14C/3H into protein in fused cells incubated in 14C-ornithine and 3H-leucine.

Lack of positive complementation in these crosses suggests that pyridoxine responsive and non-responsive patients with gyrate atrophy represent different allelic mutations of the same genetic locus coding for OKT.

relevance_reason: Maps OAT gene sequences to 10q26 and Xp11.2 and reviews 80 biochemically confirmed gyrate atrophy cases supporting autosomal recessive inheritance.

findings.statement: Barrett et al. (1987) used a cDNA clone encoding human ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) to map OAT gene sequences by somatic cell hybrids and in situ hybridization to chromosome regions 10q26 and Xp11.2.
quotes: By means of a complementary DNA clone encoding human OAT, the OAT gene sequences were mapped by somatic cell hybrids and in situ hybridization to human chromosome regions 10q26 and Xp11.2.

findings.statement: Barrett et al. (1987) reviewed 80 biochemically confirmed cases of gyrate atrophy and found that the data confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance and supported the presence of a functional OAT gene on chromosome 10.
quotes: A review of 80 biochemically confirmed cases of gyrate atrophy confirmed the autosomal recessive inheritance of this disease and supported the presence of a functional OAT gene on chromosome 10.

findings.statement: Barrett et al. (1987) noted that the X-chromosome OAT gene sequences at Xp11.2 mapped to the same region as L1.28 (Xp11.0-p11.3), a marker closely linked to X-linked recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
quotes: Interestingly, the X chromosome OAT gene sequences (Xp11.2) map to the same region as L1.28 (Xp11.0-p11.3), a marker closely linked to X-linked recessive retinitis pigmentosa.

relevance_reason: Reports the first OAT mutation (initiator codon ATG>ATA) causing gyrate atrophy in Lebanese patients, along with OAT cDNA cloning and gene structure.

findings.statement: Mitchell et al. (1988) studied 4 Lebanese patients with gyrate atrophy from 2 pedigrees. RNase A protection with antisense RNA probes showed a probe-target mismatch at the 5-prime end of the first coding exon of OAT. PCR amplification and sequencing of genomic DNA showed a G-to-A transition that changed the initiator ATG (methionine) codon to ATA, and the mutation segregated with the GA allele in both pedigrees. Initiation of translation at the closest in-frame methionine codon would truncate OAT by 138 amino acids, removing the entire mitochondrial leader sequence and 113 amino acids of the mature peptide.
quotes: performed RNase A protection experiments with RNA from four Lebanese GA patients
Sequence analysis showed a G----A transition, changing the initiator ATG (methionine) codon to ATA. This mutation segregates with the GA allele in both pedigrees.

Initiation of translation at the closest in-frame methionine codon would truncate OAT by 138 amino acids, eliminating the entire mitochondrial leader sequence and 113 amino acids of the mature peptide.

variants.as_reported: G----A transition, changing the initiator ATG (methionine) codon to ATA

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina

findings.statement: Mitchell et al. (1988) described gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina as an autosomal recessive chorioretinal degeneration caused by deficiency of the mitochondrial matrix enzyme ornithine-delta-aminotransferase (OAT).
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (GA) is an autosomal recessive chorioretinal degeneration caused by deficiency of the mitochondrial matrix enzyme, ornithine-delta-aminotransferase (OAT).

relevance_reason: Biochemical study of OKT activity and PLP responsiveness in fibroblasts from heterozygous carriers of pyridoxine-responsive and nonresponsive gyrate atrophy, relevant to carrier detection and heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Shih et al. (1988) found that cultured fibroblasts from heterozygotes for both the pyridoxine-responsive and the pyridoxine-nonresponsive variants of gyrate atrophy contained intermediate levels of ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) activity.
quotes: Fibroblasts from heterozygotes for the pyridoxine-responsive variant as well as those for the pyridoxine-nonresponsive variant contain intermediate levels of OKT activity.

phenotypes.text: intermediate ornithine ketoacid transaminase activity in heterozygote fibroblasts
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts

findings.statement: Shih et al. (1988) showed that carriers of the pyridoxine-responsive and pyridoxine-nonresponsive forms of gyrate atrophy could be distinguished by the in vitro response of fibroblast OKT activity to pyridoxal phosphate (PLP). The ratio of OKT activity at 0.04 mM PLP to that at 0 mM PLP was lowest in controls (1.18 +/- 0.18; n = 12), intermediate in pyridoxine-nonresponsive heterozygotes (1.43 +/- 0.26; n = 5), and highest in pyridoxine-responsive heterozygotes (2.20 +/- 0.14; n = 3).
quotes: These two variants can be distinguished by the in vitro responsiveness of OKT activity to pyridoxal phosphate (PLP) stimulation.

The ratios of OKT activity at 0.04 mM PLP compared with activity at 0 mM PLP were, respectively, lowest for controls (1.18 +/- 0.18; N = 12), intermediate for pyridoxine-nonresponsive heterozygotes (1.43 +/- 0.26; N = 5), and highest for pyridoxine-responsive heterozygotes (2.20 +/- 0.14; N = 3).

relevance_reason: Characterizes mutant OAT enzyme in gyrate atrophy patients, mechanism of pyridoxine response and heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Kennaway et al. (1989) characterized mutant ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) in fibroblast mitochondria from 9 patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, 4 of whom were pyridoxine-responsive, using a sensitive radiochemical assay. The apparent Km for pyridoxal phosphate (PLP) was higher in pyridoxine-responsive patients than in nonresponsive patients, whose apparent Km for PLP was normal; the apparent Km for ornithine was normal in the 7 patients studied. These data clarified the mechanism of pyridoxine response.
quotes: The apparent Km for PLP was higher in pyridoxine-responsive patients than in nonresponsive patients whose apparent Km for PLP was normal.
In contrast, the apparent Km for ornithine was normal in the seven patients studied.

to characterize the mutant enzyme in nine patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina associated with ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) deficiency, to elucidate the mechanism of response to pyridoxine in four pyridoxine-responsive patients

findings.statement: Kennaway et al. (1989) found that, surprisingly, the pyridoxine-responsive patient with the mildest clinical disease had the highest Km for PLP; however, she had the most stable OAT enzyme on heat-stability testing at 45 degrees C, which the authors presumed contributed to her milder phenotype.
quotes: Surprisingly, the responsive patient with mildest clinical disease had the highest Km for PLP. However, she had the most stable enzyme, which presumably contributed to her milder phenotype.

findings.statement: Kennaway et al. (1989) found by Western blot analysis of mitochondrial proteins with antibody to human OAT clearly detectable OAT protein in pyridoxine-responsive patients and in 2 of 5 nonresponders, but low or undetectable levels in the other 3 patients, indicating heterogeneity within as well as between the pyridoxine-responsive and nonresponsive patients with gyrate atrophy.
quotes: Western blot analyses of mitochondrial proteins, using antibody to human OAT, indicated clearly detectable OAT protein in pyridoxine-responsive patients and in two of five nonresponders, but low or undetectable levels in the other three patients.
These data clarify the mechanism of pyridoxine response and indicate heterogeneity within as well as between the pyridoxine-responsive and the nonresponsive patients with gyrate atrophy.

relevance_reason: The paper used RFLPs to show that the OAT locus on chromosome 10 segregated with gyrate atrophy and was in linkage disequilibrium with it. This is genetic evidence that a defect in the OAT gene causes GA.

findings.statement: Ramesh et al. (1988) defined 6 RFLPs at the ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) locus, all mapping to chromosome 10, with an overall heterozygosity of 83%. Using these RFLPs, they found that the OAT locus segregated concordantly with gyrate atrophy in 1 available pedigree. The RFLPs also showed significant linkage disequilibrium with GA, which the authors took as genetic evidence that a defect in the OAT structural gene causes the disorder.
quotes: The RFLPs, which are detected by noncoding single-copy probes from the OAT gene and by subclones of the HOAT1 cDNA, all map on human chromosome 10, producing an overall level of heterozygosity for the OAT locus of 83%.
Using the RFLPs, we have determined that the OAT locus segregates concordantly with GA in one available pedigree.
Furthermore, the RFLPs display significant disequilibrium with GA, providing genetic evidence implicating a defect in the OAT structural gene as the cause of this disorder.

findings.statement: Ramesh et al. (1988) suggested that the OAT RFLPs could be used for prenatal diagnosis and carrier detection in families with a previous history of gyrate atrophy. They added that the RFLPs would also allow identification of haplotypes associated with GA chromosomes.
quotes: The RFLPs for OAT are potentially applicable to prenatal diagnosis and carrier detection in families with a previous history of GA.

relevance_reason: Mutation survey of OAT in gyrate atrophy patients identifying 21 new alleles with functional characterization.

findings.statement: Brody et al. (1992) surveyed the ornithine delta-aminotransferase (OAT) genes of patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina and discovered and molecularly characterized 21 newly recognized OAT alleles, demonstrating extensive allelic heterogeneity.
quotes: We have surveyed the ornithine delta-aminotransferase genes of gyrate atrophy patients for mutations.
Using a variety of techniques, we discovered and molecularly characterized 21 newly recognized ornithine delta-aminotransferase alleles.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

findings.statement: Brody et al. (1992) determined the consequences of 21 new and 3 previously described OAT mutations on OAT mRNA, antigen, and enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts from gyrate atrophy patients: 20 of 24 alleles produced normal amounts of normally sized OAT mRNA, whereas only 2 of 24 had normal amounts of OAT antigen.
quotes: We determined the consequences of these and three previously described mutations on ornithine delta-aminotransferase mRNA, antigen, and enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts.

The majority (20/24) of these alleles produce normal amounts of normally sized ornithine delta-aminotransferase mRNA. By contrast, only 2/24 had normal amounts of ornithine delta-aminotransferase antigen.

findings.statement: Brody et al. (1992) reproduced OAT mutations by site-directed mutagenesis and expressed the mutant enzymes in Chinese hamster ovary cells, confirming that several of the mutations inactivate OAT and cause gyrate atrophy in these patients.
quotes: Reproducing these mutations by site-directed mutagenesis and expressing the mutant ornithine delta-aminotransferase in Chinese hamster ovary cells confirms that several of these mutations inactivate ornithine delta-aminotransferase and cause gyrate atrophy in these patients.

findings.statement: Brody et al. (1992) noted that inherited deficiency of ornithine delta-aminotransferase, a nuclear-encoded mitochondrial matrix enzyme, results in ornithine accumulation and a characteristic chorioretinal degeneration, gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.
quotes: Inherited deficiency of ornithine delta-aminotransferase results in ornithine accumulation and a characteristic chorioretinal degeneration, gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.

relevance_reason: The title reports that ornithine ketoacid aminotransferase activity was deficient in cultured skin fibroblasts from patients with gyrate atrophy, which is a defining biochemical finding for this entry.

findings.statement: Kennaway et al. (1977) showed that ornithine ketoacid aminotransferase activity was deficient in cultured skin fibroblasts from patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina: deficient activity of ornithine ketoacid aminotransferase in cultured skin fibroblasts.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

relevance_reason: Case report of hyperornithinemia with gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina, including the response to restricting protein intake.

findings.statement: Stoppoloni et al. (1978) reported a girl aged 3 years and 9 months with hyperornithinemia and gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina. She also had mild mental retardation, delayed language development, and speech defects.
quotes: A case of hyperornithinemia and gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina has been observed in a 3-year and 9-month-old girl.
She presented also mild mental retardation, delayed language development and speech defects.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

findings.statement: Stoppoloni et al. (1978) found that restricting protein intake to a minimum of 0.8 g/kg/day significantly lowered plasma ornithine levels in their patient with gyrate atrophy.
quotes: The restriction of protein intake to a minimum of 0.8 g/kg/day induced a significant reduction of plasma ornithine levels.

relevance_reason: Demonstrates OKT (OAT) enzyme deficiency in fibroblasts of patients with gyrate atrophy and partial deficiency in carriers, plus B6 responsiveness indicating heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Shih et al. (1978) found a virtual absence of ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) activity in cultured skin fibroblasts from 5 patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, a hyperornithinemic chorioretinal degeneration. They concluded that OKT deficiency is closely associated with the genetic defect in gyrate atrophy.
quotes: Cultured skin fibroblasts from five affected patients showed a virtual absence of ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) (L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase E.C.2.6.1.13) activity.
We conclude that OKT deficiency is closely associated with the genetic defect in gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina

phenotypes.text: virtual absence of ornithine ketoacid transaminase activity in fibroblasts
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts

findings.statement: Shih et al. (1978) found that fibroblasts from 4 carrier parents of patients with gyrate atrophy showed a 42 to 65% reduction in OKT activity, consistent with the autosomal recessive inheritance of the disorder.
quotes: Fibroblasts from four carrier parents showed a 42%-65% reduction in OKT activity.
Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina is a chorioretinal degeneration associated with hyperornithinemia with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance.

findings.statement: Shih et al. (1978) found that increasing the concentration of pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6) in the assay medium partially restored OKT activity in fibroblasts from 1 of 5 patients with gyrate atrophy, and concluded that genetic heterogeneity exists in this disease.
quotes: Increasing the concentration of pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6 in the assay media resulted in partial restoration of OKT activity in fibroblasts from one out of five patients studied.
genetic heterogeneity exists in this disease

relevance_reason: Shows that ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) activity is deficient in a patient with gyrate atrophy and intermediate in her heterozygous father, identifying the underlying enzyme defect.

findings.statement: O'Donnell et al. (1978) found that cultured fibroblasts from a female patient with gyrate atrophy of the retina did not convert uniformly 14C-labeled L-ornithine to proline. They showed that this metabolic block was caused by deficient L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase activity.
quotes: Cultured fibroblasts from a patient with gyrate atrophy of the retina do not convert L-ornithine, uniformly labeled with carbon-14, to proline.
This metabolic block is caused by deficient L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase activity in the patient.

findings.statement: O'Donnell et al. (1978) found that the father of the affected patient, an obligate heterozygote, had an intermediate level of L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase activity.
quotes: Her heterozygote father has intermediate activity of this enzyme.

relevance_reason: Clinical and muscle-pathology study of 21 patients with gyrate atrophy and hyperornithinemia. It describes type 2 fiber atrophy and tubular aggregates in muscle.

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1979) studied 21 patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina and hyperornithinemia. The patients were not weak, but type 2 muscle fibers were atrophic and had tubular aggregates in almost all of them. Both sexes were affected equally, and this was the first disease in which tubular aggregates were shown in females. The number of type 2 fibers decreased with age.
quotes: We studied 21 patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina and hyperornithinemia.
Although the patients were not weak, type 2 muscle fibers were almost universally atrophic and had tubular aggregates.
Gyrate atrophy is the first disease in which females are shown to have tubular aggregates; the sexes were affected equally.

phenotypes.text: gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

findings.statement: Sipilä et al. (1979) suggested that the muscle and eye changes in gyrate atrophy are probably related to abnormal creatine synthesis caused by the increased body pool of ornithine. They also suggested that muscle abnormalities may be present in other tapetoretinal dystrophies.
quotes: The muscle and eye changes are probably related to abnormal creatine synthesis, caused, in gyrate atrophy, by the increased body pool of ornithine; muscle abnormalities may also be present in other tapetoretinal dystrophies.

relevance_reason: Shows that patients with gyrate atrophy lack ornithine aminotransferase activity, and that an obligate heterozygote has partial activity.

findings.statement: Valle et al. (1977) measured ornithine aminotransferase (OAT; EC 2.6.1.13) activity in phytohemagglutinin-stimulated lymphocytes from a woman with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina and from her daughter. The patient's cells had no detectable OAT activity. The heterozygous daughter's cells had 44% of normal activity. Thymidine incorporation and other enzymes affected by transformation showed that the patient's cells were transformed. The authors concluded that these results demonstrated an enzyme deficiency in gyrate atrophy.
quotes: The patient's cells had no detectable ornithine aminotransferase activity, and the activity in the heterozygote's cells was 44% of normal values.

We measured the activity of ornithine aminotransferase (L-ornithine:2-oxo-acid aminotransferase, EC 2.6.1.13) in phytohemagglutinin-stimulated lymphocytes of a patient with gyrate atrophy and her daughter.
These results demonstrate an enzyme deficiency in gyrate atrophy.

phenotypes.text: absent ornithine aminotransferase activity in lymphocytes

findings.statement: Valle et al. (1977) described gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina as an inherited form of chorioretinal degeneration associated with hyperornithinemia.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina is an inherited form of chorioretinal degeneration associated with hyperornithinemia.
